headline: USD is strong against EUR, though it eased back very slightly today.
summary: Markets had penciled in only a modest pickup in German and French inflation for September, but both came in hotter than expected — Germany's harmonized inflation jumped to 3.3% and France's to 3.4%, mostly due to rising energy prices. Separately, a top Fed official said there's 'no need for urgency' on further rate hikes, cooling some of the aggressive rate-hike bets that had built up after the Fed's mid-September hike. The net effect today was a small euro uptick, but the dollar is still sitting near its highest level of the year against the euro and on track for its biggest monthly gain versus the euro in 14 months.
forYou: Right now a US dollar buys noticeably more euros than it has in over a year, so converting USD to EUR is relatively favorable compared to recent months — though that could shift around the upcoming jobs report and central bank meetings.
